why: The guess prompt comes before the answer is revealed, and cutting the unneeded Finnish-answer sentence from the setup keeps the guess honest; B gets the order right.
"One run at a time" is the literal act, while "session" is vaguer; the passive "Nobody can hand you" line is shared by both versions, so the difference is only this word.
The closing sentence 'The kit you grow on your own is the one that counts' is a slogan-style closer that adds little. Cutting it is the shorter, preferred version.
'The training runs on YOUR real work' is a neutral statement. 'YOUR real work is the material' is the more clever and abstract framing.
Shorter and plainer; 'just a draft' is cleaner than 'It often isn't. It's a draft…', cutting a low-value sentence.
Drops the count 'three', which does no memory work, so the heading becomes a frame the student controls.
The author kept the clause naming the unknown-unknowns reason for the second pass; it adds real information on why the mechanic works.
Tighter and more concrete, with no dramatic dashes or explanatory asides. Its numbers and the 'done' pushbacks give a fuller picture in fewer words.
B names what the drawing gives: recurring work has a shape that is easier to recognise drawn. A leans on 'forest before the trees', a stock metaphor, and states no content.
B opens on what the student does: ask for a ranked list. A opens on a description with a coined 'essays' frame, and the author prefers the action.
Cuts the invented concept 'The wall', which is not an industry term; the plain line description says the same thing in fewer words.
Shorter title; cutting 'Claude proposes' removes words with no loss of meaning, and word count correlates with reading speed.
B adds a closing sentence that restates the point; its 'places, not a pipeline' is a coined framing, and the author cuts low-value closers and restatements.
The author rejected 'Module 3 draws that boundary for your own repo' as an un-understandable abstraction and a forward hint, so B, which cuts it, is the better slide.
B adds 'The contrast is the material', a low-value orientation line and a clever kicker; the shorter A wins.
B cuts the 'You are not typing markdown' restatement and the forward-hint line about Phase 3 and a team PR, which are low-value sentences.
A repeats its own title as the first bullet, and its second bullet says what B's already does, so B's shorter version wins.
Bold lead-ins make the four bullets scannable, and the author uses the same bold-term pattern in his AE101 slides.
